en: *The Sutra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas of the Present Bhadrakalpa*, also titled *The Collection of the Great Mountains of Merit of All Buddhas*;
an Appendix to the Liang Record from the Kaiyuan Era.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of Joy addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, within this assembly, are there any..."
Does a bodhisattva mahāsattva who attains this samādhi also attain the eighty-four thousand gates of the pāramitās, the various gates of samādhi, and the gates of dhāraṇī?
The Buddha told King Nanda:

"In this assembly there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained this samādhi; they are also able to enter the eighty-four thousand pāramitās, as well as the various gates of samādhi and dhāraṇī."
All these bodhisattvas shall, within this Bhadrakalpa, attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi,
with the exception of the four Tathāgatas who have already attained buddhahood in this kalpa.
The Bodhisattva King of Joy again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"I only pray that the Tathāgata will proclaim the names of these bodhisattvas, which will bring great benefit and bring peace and security to the world, benefiting devas and humans; that it may protect the Buddha-dharma so that it endures for a long time, and that it may manifest the light of the Dharma for future bodhisattvas, so that their minds seeking the unsurpassed path shall never grow weary."
The Buddha told King Nanda:
“Listen attentively now, and reflect upon it well; I shall speak for you.
“So be it, World-Honored One,” he replied, “we wish to hear it with joy.”

Within this Bhadrakalpa, such are the names of the Buddhas who appear in the world.
If a person hears the names of these thousand Buddhas and does not fear error or confusion, they will certainly attain nirvana.
All those who possess wisdom, upon hearing the names of the Buddhas, should with single-mindedness refrain from negligence and practice with diligent vigor;
do not lose this opportunity, lest you fall back into the evil realms and undergo various sufferings and afflictions.

Abiding securely in the observance of precepts, following along with extensive learning, always delighting in seclusion, and being fully endowed with profound patience—such a person shall be able to encounter a thousand Buddhas.

If one upholds and recites the names of these thousand Buddhas, then the multitude of sins accumulated over immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas will be extinguished; one will certainly attain Buddhahood, as well as all *samādhis*, supernormal powers, unimpeded wisdom, various Dharma-gates, and various *dhāraṇīs*.
All the various wisdoms found in the sūtras and scriptures, and the teaching of the Dharma according to what is appropriate, should all be sought within this samādhi.

One who cultivates this samādhi should practice pure conduct, refraining from deception and remaining free from the pursuit of fame and profit; one should harbor no jealousy and practice the six points of respectful harmony. A practitioner who acts in this manner will swiftly attain the dharma of samādhi.
The Sutra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas of the Present Bhadrakalpa.
